title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two layers: (i) sketches of configurations of five marked points a,b,c,d,e on the Riemann sphere, and (ii) a tally of a dodecahedral cell structure.

(i) The configurations. The top-left sphere shows a,b,c,d,e on an equator circle. Interleaved with them are five auxiliary points: t between b and a, u between c and b, v near c and d, w near d and e, s between e and a. An arrow indicates that a is pushed off the circle. The two spheres below show the end state: a at the north pole, c,b,d,e on the equator, with meridian arcs from a. A hatched triangle marks a cell or chamber. The bottom row repeats this deformation. In it, a leaves the circle, the remaining four (plus auxiliary points s, α) stay on it, and a point descends to the opposite pole.

The central drawing is a solid polyhedral cell. Its top face is the circle carrying d,v,c,u,b,t,s,e. Its downward edges and the faces below are labelled (a),(b),(c),(d),(e), i.e. by which marked point is moving or degenerate. Vertices s and t are distinguished, and a hatched triangle again marks a fundamental chamber. The small lens at upper right has vertices s and t, boundary arcs labelled d,c (top) and b,e (bottom), an interior point α and a hatched sector. It looks like a 2-cell, a 'bigon' between s and t, cut out by the circle arcs.

The most plausible reading is this. Grothendieck is building an explicit, symmetric cell decomposition of a space of configurations of 5 points on P^1. That means M_{0,5}, or a variant with auxiliary points, cut along the loci where 4 or 5 points are cocircular. The aim is to read off generators and relations of the genus-0, 5-point Teichmüller groupoid (the 'S0 T' of the folder title). This fits the previous page, which lists transition maps (41), (42) between base points and groupoids Π_X, Π_P attached to polygons and Riemann surfaces.

(ii) The dodecahedral count. On the right he defines sets attached to 'bidodécagones'. 'Bi' plausibly marks a dimension-2 polygon, i.e. the dodecahedron; it is crossed out once.
- R, the 'repères généraux' (flags): 120.
- F, faces: 12.
- A, edges: 30.
- S, vertices: 20.
Arrows R→F, R→A, R→S show the flag set fibring over faces, edges and vertices: 120 = 12·10 = 30·4 = 20·6.

The check 2×(6+15+10) = 62 = 12+30+20 counts cells via symmetry axes: 6 five-fold, 15 two-fold and 10 three-fold axes, each meeting the sphere in two antipodal poles. Equivalently, 6, 15, 10 are the face, edge and vertex counts of the hemi-dodecahedron (the dodecahedron modulo the antipodal map, a cell structure on RP^2). The 120 flags form a torsor under the full icosahedral group A_5×Z/2, the same order as S_5, which permutes the five marked points.

The suggested aim is to match the Teichmüller-groupoid cell structure for five points with dodecahedral/icosahedral combinatorics. Two facts support this: the 10 vertices and 15 edges of the hemi-dodecahedron's 1-skeleton (the Petersen graph) are exactly the 10 boundary divisors D_ij and 15 boundary points of \bar M_{0,5}, and A_5 sits inside S_5. The page does not make this identification explicit.
errors: Terminology is unstable: 'bidodécagones' is used for faces and flags, then 'bi' is struck out for edges. Whether the object is the dodecahedron or a 12-cell complex built from configurations of points is not settled on the page.

The identification between the configuration-space cell structure (central drawing) and the dodecahedron is not stated or justified. Note that the real locus \bar M_{0,5}(R) is tiled by 12 pentagons with 30 edges but 15 vertices (χ = -3), not 20. So if the dodecahedron is meant as a model of \bar M_{0,5}(R), a double cover or a different space must be intended.

ideas.what: Cell decomposition of the configuration space of 5 points on P^1 by cocircularity strata: all points on a circle, one point leaving the circle. Chambers are labelled by the moving point and used to compute Teichmüller-groupoid generators.
ideas.modern_name: Cell/stratified decompositions of M_{0,5}; Teichmüller groupoid / Lego of genus 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); Lochak–Schneps, Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov for the Teichmüller tower in genus 0
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, pentagon relation), in outline only

ideas.what: Flag/face/edge/vertex count of the dodecahedron (120/12/30/20), with the check via 6+15+10 rotation axes (equivalently, the hemi-dodecahedron).
ideas.modern_name: Flag-transitive regular polytope combinatorics; icosahedral group A_5×C_2; hemi-dodecahedron

ideas.what: Implicit link between S_5 symmetry of five marked points (order 120) and dodecahedral flags (order 120); the Petersen-graph count (10, 15) matches the boundary of \bar M_{0,5}.
ideas.modern_name: Petersen graph as boundary complex of \bar M_{0,5}; del Pezzo quintic surface with S_5 action; Clebsch/icosahedral connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical/known (Hirzebruch on Clebsch cubic and icosahedron; Kapranov, Devadoss on tessellations of \bar M_{0,n}(R))

missed.claim: Grothendieck seems to be fitting a dodecahedral (icosahedrally symmetric) cell structure, with 120 flags matching the 120 = |S_5| symmetries, to the configuration space of five points on the sphere, as a model for the genus-0, 5-point Teichmüller groupoid. The identification is left implicit and its precise form is unclear. Related facts (Petersen graph as boundary complex, 12-pentagon tiling of \bar M_{0,5}(R)) are known, so novelty is doubtful.
missed.quote: R repères des bidodécagones (120) généraux ... F faces (12) ... A arêtes (30) ... S sommets (20) ... 2×(6+15+10) = 62
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an S_5-equivariant, Platonic-solid model for base points and paths of π_1(M_{0,5}), relevant to the pentagon relation in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. It is of mostly historical interest, since equivalent combinatorics now exist in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is exploratory sketching: configurations of 5 points on a sphere plus a routine dodecahedron count. The suggested link between dodecahedral flags and S_5-symmetric cell structures on M_{0,5} is suggestive, but it is not made explicit, and related combinatorics (Petersen graph, 12-pentagon tiling) are well known.
transcription_corrections: Top-left sphere: the marks near e read 'w' with a crossed point 'x' (w, x, e), not 'w e'.
The right-hand list is a diagram: arrows go from R to F, A and S. 'repères des bidodécagones (120) généraux' is the label of R.
Under A: the original reads 'arêtes [des struck] des [bi struck?]dodécagones (30)', i.e. the prefix 'bi' is crossed out here only.
Lens figure, upper right: vertices s (left) and t (right); top arcs labelled c, d; bottom arcs labelled e, b; interior point α; hatched sector near c–s.
Bottom figures: labels include α beside a and s on the equator; in the last figure a sits on the circle next to b, with an upward arrow from the lower point.
